title: Boundary Element Modeling of Thermoplasmonic Ag–TiO₂ Core–Shell Nanostructures: Coupling and Interfacial Heat Transfer
content: Thermoplasmonic core shell nanostructures provide an effective platform for localized optical heating, but accurate prediction of their thermal response requires a computational framework capable of distinguishing electromagnetic interactions from thermal field superposition while accounting for heat transfer across material interfaces. This study develops a three dimensional multiregion boundary element formulation and verification protocol for silver titanium dioxide core shell nanostructures embedded in an unbounded host medium. The electromagnetic problem is formulated using a surface integral representation with Rao Wilton Glisson discretization, allowing multiple material interfaces and exterior radiation conditions to be treated directly. Optical absorption is independently evaluated through volumetric electromagnetic loss and boundary Poynting flux, providing a consistent and auditable transfer of absorbed optical energy to the thermal model. Transient heat conduction is formulated through a modified Helmholtz representation and solved using a dual reciprocity boundary element approach that incorporates finite thermal boundary resistance at the silver titanium dioxide and titanium dioxide host interfaces. A controlled decomposition procedure is introduced to distinguish temperature changes caused by thermal field overlap from those associated with electromagnetic modification of optical absorption. Verification is supported through sphere based electromagnetic controls, analytical transient thermal benchmarks, interface resistance assessment, and reconstruction of a published reference geometry. The study establishes a reproducible and conservation based computational framework for the rigorous analysis of coupled electromagnetic and thermal transport in coated plasmonic nanostructures, with emphasis on numerical consistency, energy conservation, interfacial effects, source transfer accuracy, and systematic verification before predictive nanoscale simulations are undertaken.
